reproduction_target: Joint single-cell whole-genome + whole-transcriptome (SMART-PTA) reconstruction of somatic clonal evolution in phenotypically normal esophagus from four aged donors. Computational target: Ultima Genomics scWGS processing (samtools merge, Picard DownsampleSam, UG-tuned DeepVariant/Parabricks), GLnexus joint genotyping, ANNOVAR annotation, single-cell QC (SingleCheck), somatic variant calling with a modified Sequoia + treemut, a custom linked-read/XGBoost PTA-error classifier, maximum-likelihood single-cell phylogeny with a distributed CellPhy (cloudCellphy), branch-length mutation mapping, MEGA RelTime time-calibration, mutation-burden and clade counting, lineage-through-time (ape/phytools), PATH phylogenetic cross-correlation, mutational-signature decomposition (MutationalPatterns + SigProfiler, COSMIC v3.4), CADD/dNdScv driver analysis, SHAPEIT5+HMMCopy LOH/CNLOH calling, Ginkgo CNV calling, targeted deep-sequencing variant calling (BWA/Picard/GATK), and the scG2P Mission Bio DNA+RNA genotype-to-phenotype analysis (Mosaic, Seurat). RNA arm: FastP/STAR/HTSeq/TRUST4 nextflow workflow plus scanpy/scVI embedding, Leiden clustering and diffusion pseudotime. Wet-lab steps (DLD-1 clonal expansion, SMART-PTA reagent/liquid-handling optimization, biopsy collection and FACS, hybridization-capture panel, Tapestri encapsulation, donor recruitment/IRB) are W and out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 full-text HTML Methods section (retrieved by curl; WebFetch of both .source.xml and the .full page returned HTTP 403/429, and the paper is not in Europe PMC full text — abstract only, inEPMC=N). 28 computational steps and 6 wet-lab steps were enumerated. The paper's Methods carry an unusually dense set of exact prose version pins (FastP 0.23.4, STAR 2.7.1a, HTSeq 0.12.3, TRUST4 1.0.13, Python 3.11, scanpy 1.9.8, scVI 1.1.1, samtools 1.19/1.21, BCFtools 1.9/1.15.0/1.15.1, bedtools 2.31.0, GLnexus 1.4.1, Cutadapt 2.10, BWA MEM 0.7.17, Picard 2.18.17, DeepVariant 4.5.0 via Parabricks, treemut 1.1, treeio 1.14.4, dplyr 1.1.3, tidyr 1.3.1, tibble 3.2.1, vroom 1.6.5, dndscv 0.0.1.0, SHAPEIT5 5.1.0, Seurat 4.0.0, MEGA 11), but roughly half the steps also invoke at least one tool with no version at all (Ginkgo, HMMCopy, XGBoost, SigProfiler, MutationalPatterns, castor, ape, phytools, PATH, Quartet, deconstructSigs, Rsamtools, SingleCheck, CellPhy in the DLD-1 benchmark, Mission Bio Mosaic, and R itself), which caps those steps at NI on the version axis. Two proprietary/pre-release dependencies appear: Ultima Genomics proprietary demultiplex/trim/map software, and a 'pre-release version of NVIDIA Parabricks Deepvariant ... based on v. 4.1.2'. Code availability names four GitHub repositories; one of them (github.com/jzinno/rsoRNA, the RNA analysis code) returns HTTP 404 — link rot at the time of assessment. The two Nextflow repositories that do resolve (darkshore, cloudCellphy) both ship a docker/ directory, a Docker-build CI badge, and a README instruction that 'the pipelines will automatically pull the required containers when run', which is a container-based environment CLAIM (not a verified digest) and is why capture_claim is env_lock_claimed and stage2_candidate is true.

steps.label: Wet-lab: DLD-1 (ATCC CCL-221) in vitro single-cell evolutionary model — four months of serial single-cell cloning across three filial generations, cryopreservation, flow sorting into 96-well plates, PTA whole-genome amplification (ResolveDNA v1, BioSkryb) and Kapa HyperPlus library prep
Wet-lab: conversion of DLD-1 Illumina libraries to Ultima Genomics libraries and sequencing at NYGC (~30x/cell), plus matched Illumina NovaSeq6000 sequencing of F1/F2/H1/H2 at >15x

Wet-lab: SMART-PTA protocol development — ResolveOME v1 reagents at 0.25x volume on a Mantis Liquid Dispenser (Formulatrix), bead-based cDNA/PTA separation, G.PURE (Cytena) automated cleanup, NovaSeq6000 PE150 cDNA sequencing and UG100 WGS at 15x target
Wet-lab: regional esophageal biopsy sampling (2 mm forceps, proximal/distal sites 3 cm apart), Dispase/Trypsin or Liberase dissociation, EPCAM+/CD45+ sorting into 384-well plates on a BD Symphony S6

Wet-lab: targeted deep sequencing of a 7-gene driver panel (NOTCH1/2/3, TP53, FAT1, PPM1D, ZFP36L2) with a custom xGen Custom Hybridization Capture Panel (IDT), 2x tiling (1x for NOTCH2 and FAT1), NovaSeq6000 PE150

Wet-lab: scG2P single-cell targeted genotype-to-phenotype assay — custom DNA hotspot panel + 58-transcript RNA panel, 100,000 EPCAM+ cells on Mission Bio Tapestri, NovaSeq6000 PE150; plus donor recruitment and IRB approvals (Columbia AAAS4603, Kyoto G0645)

Ultima Genomics DLD-1 scWGS processing: per-cell CRAM merge with samtools merge, empirical depth estimate from primary alignments x mean read length of the first million reads, downsampling to 15x with Picard DownsampleSam, and GVCF/VCF generation with a customized UG-optimized DeepVariant — no version given for samtools, Picard, or the customized DeepVariant

Matched Illumina DLD-1 scWGS processing: Cutadapt (v. 2.10) trimming, BWA MEM (v. 0.7.17) alignment to hg38, Picard (v. 2.18.17) duplicate marking and downsampling to 15x, DeepVariant with default parameters (v. 4.5.0 via parabricks) — covered in kind by the public scVC-il.nf workflow in github.com/jzinno/darkshore

Benchmark of UG vs Illumina scWGS variant calling: ANNOVAR (June 2020 version) annotation against dbSNP 150, germline/somatic partitioning against a published DLD-1 colony, R set intersection, trinucleotide context extraction with Rsamtools scanFa, and 96-context SBS fitting with deconstructSigs — Rsamtools, deconstructSigs and R itself carry no version

DLD-1 in vitro phylogeny reconstruction and benchmark: joint genotyping of 16 single-cell GVCFs with GLnexus (v1.4.1), CellPhy tree inference with the GT10+FO+E model, and topology comparison against the known clone genealogy using the R package Quartet — CellPhy and Quartet versions not stated in this step

Standard-PTA+RNA vs SMART-PTA benchmark: SingleCheck (https://github.com/tamaraprieto/SingleCheck) run with the N parameter on UG-processed BAMs, coverage breadth/mappability/uniformity (1/MAD over 10 Mb windows), transcript counts and ribosomal/mitochondrial fractions, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum comparison on 50 randomly selected cells per protocol — SingleCheck has no version/tag/release (last push 2020-11-13) and the random 50-cell selection has no seed

scRNA-seq preprocessing (scRNA.nf in github.com/jzinno/darkshore): FastP (v. 0.23.4) TSO and >=10-base homopolymer trimming with default filters, STAR (v. 2.7.1a) two-pass alignment to hg38 with stranded 'no', HTSeq (v. 0.12.3) gene-level counting with default settings, matrix consolidation in bash, and TCR reconstruction with TRUST4 (v. 1.0.13) against hg38 references

scRNA normalization, batch correction and cell typing: Python (v. 3.11) with scanpy (v. 1.9.8), knee-point filter at 200K read counts, top-1,000 highly variable genes (Seurat v3 flavor), scVI (v. 1.1.1) embeddings with donor / sequencing batch / 384-well / 96-well categorical covariates, scanpy.pp.neighbors graph, Leiden clustering, UMAP, and marker-gene-based cell-type assignment — the cited code repository github.com/jzinno/rsoRNA returns HTTP 404

Diffusion pseudotime analysis: scanpy.tl.diffmap over the scVI cell embeddings followed by scanpy.tl.dpt (scanpy v. 1.9.8, Python v. 3.11) — root cell selection not stated, code repository (rsoRNA) dead

DNA-seq processing and variant calling: demultiplexing/trimming/hg38 mapping with Ultima Genomics proprietary software, per-cell CRAM merge and read-group reheadering with samtools (v. 1.19), SingleCheck QC with the N option, GATK MarkDuplicates plus a pre-release NVIDIA Parabricks DeepVariant based on v. 4.1.2 on L40S GPUs, GLNexus joint genotyping with a UG-specific configuration, and ANNOVAR (June 2020, -protocol refGene, dbNSFP v4.2c, COSMIC v70, dbSNP avsnp150, ExAC v0.3, ClinVar 20220320)

Somatic variant identification: the original Sequoia script (accessed April 2024) modified to accept interval data and to compute outgroup-vs-ingroup mutation-placement significance using code from the treemut (v. 1.1) R package, then BCFtools (v. 1.15.1) normalization and filtering (QUAL<20 removal; cell filters on breadth, MAD, depth, unmapped fraction; avsnp150/outgroup/germline q>0.00005 removal; recurrence and mean-depth>30 exclusion; retention at Sequoia rho>0.5 or rho>0.65)

Germline variant selection and per-cell recall calculation: BCFtools (v. 1.9) filtering on dbSNP presence, germline quality >0.00005 and mean depth >3, heterozygous selection on GT=het with allele frequency 0.25-0.75, then per-cell reference/alternative read extraction and computation of the proportion of heterozygous sites with >=1 alternative read

Large-scale phylogenetic reconstruction: HPC-distributed CellPhy ('0.9.3git CellPhy branch') via github.com/jzinno/cloudCellphy on the somatic-SNV VCF with the GT10+FO+E model, 100 bootstrap replicates, and variant filters (present in <2 cells, >50% missing genotypes, mean per-cell depth <=9, and exclusion of chromosome 9 to avoid CNLOH-induced artifacts)

SMART-PTA error classifier: linked-read haplotype counting from single-cell BAMs with a custom (unpublished) python script after edit-distance/base-quality/mapping-quality filters, BED/VCF intersection with bedtools (v. 1.9), REDI RNA-editing database annotation, features adapted from PTATO (replication timing, repeat distance, gene distance/strand, 200-kb window, Loess VAF residual, binomial P), R-side Shannon-diversity metrics, basic and stringent true/false-positive labelling, and an XGBoost model with 5-fold cross-validation used to filter variants at 0.5/0.9 error-probability thresholds

Calculation of phylogenetic branch lengths: mutation mapping with the treemut (v. 1.1) R package in two rounds (before and after the error classifier), removal of cells with >0.25 singleton avsnp150 sites, and additional manual cell filtering where cell breadth correlated negatively with branch length

Phylogenetic time-calibration: MEGA (v. 11) command-line RelTime with a calibration file constraining epithelial/immune ancestral nodes (minTime = donor age + 9 months, maxTime = donor age; root set to fertilization age)

Somatic SNV mutation burden per cell: root-to-tip branch-length summation with get_all_distances_to_root from the castor R package, corrected by per-cell variant-calling recall percentages — castor version not stated and the displayed correction formula is rendered as an image in the preprint

Phylogenetic clade (clone) counting: temporal cut-off at birth (0.75 time units from the root), tree-to-data.frame conversion and node selection with dplyr (v. 1.1.3), tidyr (v. 1.3.1) and treeio (v. 1.14.4), removal of nested internal nodes, and enumeration of tip descendants with cell-type annotation

Lineage-through-time analysis: ltt.plot.coords from the ape package on pruned per-cell-type/region subtrees (drop.tip from treeio v. 1.14.4, minimum three tips), GAM fitting of proportional lineage counts, gammaStat gamma-statistic with a two-sided normal approximation, and the MCCR test from the phytools R package with rho=0.005 and nsim=100 — ape and phytools carry no version and MCCR has no seed

Phylogenetic cross-correlation between immune and epithelial cells: one_node_tree_dist phylogenetic weight matrix from the PATH R package, catMat presence/absence matrix of EPCAM+/CD45+ labels with percent unmapped reads as a negative control, and Z scores from PATH xcor — PATH version not stated

Phylogenetic correlation of anatomic esophageal regions: compartment-specific subtrees, inverse phylogenetic distance weight matrices from PATH inv_tree_dist, xcor Z scores against anatomical distance from the incisors, and error bars from five random tip partitions per compartment — PATH version not stated and the random partitioning has no seed

Epithelial mutational-signature analysis over time: immune-branch pruning with treeio (v. 1.14.4) and tibble (v. 3.2.1), Sequoia SNV import with vroom (v. 1.6.5), early/middle/late branch classification by divergence time (internal >=40 y, internal <40 y, external), branch-midpoint age correction, 96-context profile construction with the MutationalPatterns function mut.to.sigs.input against GRCh38, and SigProfiler fitting to COSMIC (hg38, v3.4) SBS1/5/40a, SBS4/92/16 and SBS40b/40c negative controls — MutationalPatterns and SigProfiler versions not stated

Proportion of mutated vs wild-type cells: CADD PHRED annotation of somatic SNVs in 83 previously analyzed esophageal genes using site-specific tables extracted from the CADD database (hg38, v1.7) with an unpublished bash script, ANNOVAR exonic synonymous/non-synonymous filtering, restriction to the 28 positively selected driver genes, and per-cell mutation counting from branch identifiers — R and the extraction script carry no version and the script is not published

dN/dS analysis: dndscv (v. 0.0.1.0) R package with hg38 covariates, per-patient gene rates via gene_list = TTN, FAT1, TP53, confidence intervals from geneci with the same gene_list, and random downsampling of the gene presence/absence matrix to 608 cells per donor with all-zero rows removed — no seed for the downsampling

Loss-of-heterozygosity (CNLOH) calling: SHAPEIT5 (v5.1.0) phasing of MAF>=0.1% germline variants in ~25 cM chunks with phase_common_static, a genetic map and a high-coverage 1000 Genomes reference panel, ligation with ligate_static, indexing with BCFtools (v1.15.0), then HMMCopy HMMSegment with mu at the 50th/99th VAF quantiles and kappa=(0.7,0.3)x1000, eta=(50,5)x10,000 — HMMCopy version not stated and the 1000 Genomes panel build is not pinned

CNV calling with Ginkgo: samtools (v1.21) MAPQ>=40 filtering, BED conversion with bedtools (v2.31.0), the analyze.sh script shipped with Ginkgo run with default parameters including GC correction and segmentation but with hg38 instead of hg19, at 500-kb and 50-kb bin sizes, using hg38 support files the authors constructed themselves following the hg19 precalculated file structure — Ginkgo has no version and the custom hg38 support files are not deposited

Targeted deep-sequencing analysis of the driver panel: CutAdapt adapter removal, BWA MEM alignment to hg38, Picard SortSam and MergeWithMarkDuplicates, two-step GATK base-quality recalibration, per-donor GATK HaplotypeCaller in GVCF mode and joint genotyping with GATK GenotypeGVCFs — none of CutAdapt, BWA, Picard or GATK carries a version in this step and no known-sites resource is named for BQSR

scG2P DNA arm: Mission Bio Mosaic pipeline for adapter trimming and cell calling, GATK HaplotypeCaller variant calling, GVCF merge into a Mission Bio object, variant-level and cell-level filtering (>=10 total reads/cell, >=3 alternate reads, GATK genotyping quality >30, variants genotyped in >=50% of cells, cells with >=50% informative genotypes), and NOTCH1 LOH determination from five intronic SNPs verified on GnomAD — Mosaic and GATK versions and the GnomAD release are not stated

scG2P RNA arm: FASTQ processing with the custom script PRIMR (https://github.com/Theob0t/PRIMR) to build cell-by-transcript matrices, then Seurat (v. 4.0.0) analysis with a >=50 reads/cell filter, Center-Log-Ratio normalization, dimension reduction and clustering, and cell-cycling/differentiation scores via AddModuleScore on previously described gene lists

headline.static_readiness: 0/28 (0%) — stage1 ceiling only, no R★ (R★ needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 11/28 computational steps (C2, C6, C7, C8, C11, C12, C14, C15, C17, C23, C28) — those are the steps in which every named tool carries an exact prose version pin (or, for C12, a named CellPhy git branch). The remaining 17/28 steps cap at NI because at least one tool in the step has no version at all: Ginkgo, HMMCopy, XGBoost, SigProfiler, MutationalPatterns, castor, ape, phytools, PATH, Quartet, deconstructSigs, Rsamtools, SingleCheck, Mission Bio Mosaic, the customized UG DeepVariant, CutAdapt/BWA/Picard/GATK in the targeted-panel step, and R itself. Two steps additionally carry non-reconstructable dependencies: C9 uses Ultima Genomics proprietary demultiplex/trim/map software plus a 'pre-release version of NVIDIA Parabricks Deepvariant ... based on v. 4.1.2', and C27 uses the vendor Mission Bio Mosaic pipeline. Every step is also capped on the Data axis at 1 because the single-cell genomics data are only promised ('will be deposited in EGA. Accession codes will be made available upon publication') — no accession exists at assessment time. Under stage-2 execution the upper bound could rise if the containers referenced by the darkshore/cloudCellphy READMEs turn out to be digest-pinned and to cover the R/python stacks, which is exactly the check this paper is being flagged for.
headline.coverage: 28 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 Methods section. 6 wet-lab steps (DLD-1 clonal expansion + PTA, UG/Illumina sequencing, SMART-PTA protocol development, biopsy collection and FACS, hybridization-capture panel, Tapestri scG2P + donor recruitment/IRB) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 28/34 (82%) of enumerated steps.

gaps.where: Code and Data Availability — 'The single-cell genomics data will be deposited in EGA. Accession codes will be made available upon publication.'
gaps.missing: No data accession exists at assessment time. The scWGS (Ultima Genomics), scRNA-seq, targeted deep-sequencing and scG2P Tapestri datasets for all four donors and for the DLD-1 in vitro model are undeposited, so every one of the 28 computational steps is capped at data=1 and none can be started by a third party. The reused DLD-1 colony Illumina control is cited only by publication (ref 127), with no SRA run accession given in Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the single-cell genomics data to EGA and publish the study/dataset accessions plus the DAC contact and application path in the Data Availability statement; list the SRA run accession for the reused DLD-1 colony control; deposit non-identifiable intermediates (the somatic-SNV VCFs, the per-donor Newick trees, the gene-by-cell count matrices) openly so downstream steps can be started without controlled-access approval.

gaps.where: Code and Data Availability — 'RNA analysis: github.com/jzinno/rsoRNA'
gaps.missing: The RNA analysis repository returns HTTP 404 (verified 2026-07-27, unauthenticated). This is the code cited for steps C7 (scanpy/scVI normalization, batch correction, Leiden clustering, marker-based cell typing) and C8 (diffusion pseudotime) — the entire transcriptomic cell-state analysis that the paper's genotype-to-phenotype claims rest on. No authoritative mirror was found within the bounded check (the sibling landau-lab organization repo landau-lab/smartpta resolves, but is the SMART-PTA nextflow bundle, not rsoRNA).
gaps.how_to_close: Restore or rename-redirect the rsoRNA repository, or move the RNA analysis code into landau-lab/smartpta, tag a release and archive it to Zenodo/Software Heritage with a DOI so the citation cannot rot again.

gaps.where: 17 of 28 computational steps (C1, C3, C4, C5, C9, C10, C13, C16, C18, C19, C20, C21, C22, C24, C25, C26, C27)
gaps.missing: At least one tool per step has no version: the customized UG DeepVariant (C1), Rsamtools/deconstructSigs/R (C3), CellPhy and Quartet in the DLD-1 benchmark (C4), SingleCheck (C5, C9), Sequoia ('accessed April 2024' is a date, not a version) (C10), XGBoost and the custom linked-read python script (C13), castor (C16), ape and phytools (C18), PATH (C19, C20), MutationalPatterns and SigProfiler (C21), the CADD extraction bash script and R (C22), HMMCopy (C24), Ginkgo (C25), CutAdapt/BWA/Picard/GATK in the targeted-panel arm (C26), and Mission Bio Mosaic (C27). R and Bioconductor release versions are never stated anywhere in Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a versions table to Methods or Supplementary giving an exact version (or commit SHA) for every tool and package invoked, including R, Bioconductor release, and each R package, and record sessionInfo()/pip freeze output for the R and python analyses.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock, requirements.txt or container digest is claimed in the paper itself. The two resolvable Nextflow repositories (darkshore, cloudCellphy) each ship a docker/ directory and a Docker-build CI badge, and darkshore's README states 'The pipelines will automatically pull the required containers when run' with minimum-version requirements 'Nextflow 22.10.4+' and 'Singularity 3.8.6+' — floating lower bounds, and the container references are not shown as digests at the README prose level. The R and python analysis stacks (treemut, treeio, castor, ape, phytools, PATH, dndscv, HMMCopy, Ginkgo, MutationalPatterns, SigProfiler, Seurat, scanpy, scVI, XGBoost) are outside any container claim entirely — they are described only as prose version pins.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a digest-pinned container manifest (or conda-lock/pixi lockfile with interpreter, channel and platform declared) covering both the Nextflow steps and the downstream R/python analysis stacks, replace the '+' minimum-version requirements with exact tested versions, and reference the capture from Code Availability.

gaps.where: C13 (SMART-PTA error classifier), C22 (CADD site-table extraction), C10 (modified Sequoia), C25 (Ginkgo hg38 support files)
gaps.missing: Several load-bearing custom artifacts are described but not published: the custom python script that counts linked reads from single-cell BAMs, the R code computing the linked-read metrics, the trained XGBoost classifier and its feature table, the modifications to the Sequoia script (interval support plus the outgroup/ingroup placement significance calculation), the bash script used to extract per-gene site tables from the CADD database, and the hg38 support files the authors constructed for Ginkgo. None of these appear in the four cited repositories, whose scope is scWGA QC, variant calling/joint genotyping, the distributed tree search and (dead link) RNA analysis.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the classifier training code, feature matrix and serialized model, the modified Sequoia fork (as a fork with visible diff), the CADD extraction script and the Ginkgo hg38 support files, with checksums, alongside the existing repositories.

gaps.where: C5 (random 50-cell selection per protocol), C12 (100 bootstrap replicates and multiple ML tree initializations), C13 (XGBoost 5-fold cross-validation), C18 (MCCR nsim=100), C20 (five random tip partitions per compartment), C23 (downsampling to 608 cells per donor)
gaps.missing: No RNG seeds are reported for any of the stochastic steps, and the code for most of them is not published, so the reported bootstrap supports, gamma-statistic MCCR P values, classifier probabilities, correlation error bars and per-donor dN/dS estimates are reproducible only distributionally.
gaps.how_to_close: Fix and report RNG seeds for the cell subsampling, tip partitioning, cross-validation and MCCR simulations, and publish the scripts that consume them so the seed can be shown to be consumed.

gaps.where: External reference resources across C3, C9, C13, C21, C22, C24, C27
gaps.missing: Reference resources are pinned in prose only (or not at all) and no download rule is visible at Stage 1: dbSNP 150 / avsnp150, ANNOVAR June 2020 with dbNSFP v4.2c, COSMIC v70, ExAC v0.3, ClinVar 20220320, COSMIC SBS v3.4 (hg38), CADD hg38 v1.7 are prose-pinned; the REDI RNA-editing database (http://srv00.recas.ba.infn.it/atlas/), the 1000 Genomes high-coverage phasing reference panel and genetic map used by SHAPEIT5, the hg38 TRUST4 reference resources, the darkshore 'reference data bundle' pulled by resources/ref_setup.sh, and the GnomAD release used to verify NOTCH1 intronic SNPs carry no version at all. Whether the workflows fetch versioned artifacts (class A) or consume user-supplied local paths (class B) or rolling resources (class C) cannot be decided without reading the Nextflow code — that is a Stage-2 check.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin every reference resource to a versioned accession/DOI or digest inside the workflow's download rules (not only in prose), publish checksums for the reference data bundle produced by ref_setup.sh, and state the GnomAD and 1000 Genomes releases used.

gaps.where: C9 (DNA-seq processing and variant calling), C1 (UG DLD-1 processing), C27 (scG2P DNA arm)
gaps.missing: Three steps depend on vendor software that a third party cannot obtain or pin: Ultima Genomics proprietary demultiplexing/trimming/mapping software, a 'customized version of DeepVariant, optimized for UG sequencing data' and a 'pre-release version of NVIDIA Parabricks Deepvariant ... based on v. 4.1.2' (a pre-release build is by definition not a distributable version), and the Mission Bio Mosaic pipeline. Under the rubric's proprietary ceiling these steps cannot exceed NI.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact vendor software builds used and whether they are obtainable (licence route, container registry), and either release the UG-optimized DeepVariant model/binary or document an open-source equivalent path with a concordance comparison.

gaps.where: C14 (branch-length recalculation) and Supplementary Fig. 2A cell filtering
gaps.missing: Cell filtering at the branch-length step is explicitly manual: 'Further cell filtering was manually performed when a negative correlation was observed between the cell breadth and branch length likely caused by exogenous contamination.' No threshold, no list of excluded cells, and no script are given, so the final tree backbone cannot be regenerated deterministically.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the list of manually excluded cells per donor (or a deterministic rule with a threshold) and the code that applies it.

gaps.missing: Recorded as an internal inconsistency rather than a defect claim: bedtools is cited as 'v. 1.9' in two places, but bedtools has no 1.9 release (1.9 is a BCFtools/samtools version line; bedtools is at 2.x, and the CNV step correctly cites bedtools v2.31.0). The version string as printed cannot be resolved to an installable artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: Correct the bedtools version strings in the SMART-PTA error classifier and germline sections to the actual 2.x release used.

gaps.missing: No gap — recorded for completeness. Six wet-lab steps (DLD-1 serial cloning and PTA, UG/Illumina library conversion and sequencing, SMART-PTA reagent and liquid-handling optimization, biopsy collection/dissociation/FACS, xGen capture panel, Tapestri scG2P and donor recruitment under Columbia AAAS4603 / Kyoto G0645) are out of computational-reproduction scope and excluded from |S|.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a — OOS by scope definition. A protocols.io deposition of the SMART-PTA workflow would nonetheless raise wet-lab documentation quality, since the protocol is a central methodological claim of the paper.
